reviewed_behaviors.behavior: same-session navigation does not hide password settings
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The security form has uniquely labeled password inputs “Current password”, “New password”, and “Confirm password”, and a button “Update password”; submitting an empty current-password field must display the visible application message “Current password is required”. A failure with an incorrect current password and confirmation “does-not-match” must display the corresponding current-password or confirmation error and leave the old credentials usable. Each password-change scenario starts with its own verified account in the stated credential state and a different compliant candidate password. “Password and authentication” is the security page in account Settings used to change the current account credentials; the change affects only the current account's password record and does not alter any other accounts or resources outside the session. The user must provide the current password, a new password compliant with the REQ-1 password rules, and a character-for-character identical confirmation password; all three fields are required. The system validates the change, prevents unauthorized updates, and applies the new password to subsequent sign-in attempts. If the current password is incorrect, the new password is noncompliant, the confirmation does not match, or any field is missing, the system displays the reason in the corresponding field and does not modify the credentials; the applicable visible message is “Current password is incorrect”, “Password confirmation does not match”, or “Current password is required”. The old password remains valid and the new password must not work for sign-in. After a successful update, the page displays “Password updated”, the new password is immediately used for subsequent password-based sign-ins, and the old password must no longer work for new sign-ins.

Seed password-change values are `New-password-456!` for the successful update and
`Required-password-789!` for the missing-current-password scenario.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-password-settings.png)

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: public navigation remains available during repository loading
reviewed_behaviors.basis:

Each result has a link named exactly with the repository name, and opens a heading displaying “organization name/repository name”. Returning with browser Back keeps the public result available; filtering by the exact private repository name never exposes its link to a visitor. The seed organization has a public repository and a distinct private repository inaccessible to visitors. The system displays only the names, descriptions, visibility, and update times of repositories visible to the current user; clicking a result opens that repository's overview. Visitors can view public repositories on a public organization overview page; signed-in accounts can see only repositories for which they have read permission on the Repositories tab of the organization overview. reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on the persisted objects. The sign-in page is the form on the account-access page containing “Username or email”, “Password”, and “Sign in”. A “session” is the current-browser login record saved after successful account authentication, represented in the frontend by the upper-right account menu and access to protected pages. The visitor enters a username or email and a password and submits the form. After successful authentication, the system stores a session with a unique session identifier, account identifier, and active status, then redirects to the workspace accessible to that user; the session remains valid after refreshing or reopening the workspace, and subsequent protected organization, repository, and work-item requests must use this session to determine the current user.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: homepage provides direct Sign up and rejected registration clears passwords
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
The registration page is the form opened by the unique link named “Create an account” from the sign-in page. The form contains exactly one textbox labeled “Username”, one textbox labeled “Email”, one password input labeled “Password”, one password input labeled “Confirm password”, one initially unchecked checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and one enabled button named “Create account”. The username and email identify the account, while passwords must not be echoed on the page. This product directly marks the email of a successfully registered account as verified and does not provide a subsequent email-verification page. The visitor enters a unique username, email, password, and matching confirmation, checks “Agree to the terms”, and activates “Create account”. The username must consist of 1 to 39 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens (`-`) and must not begin or end with a hyphen; after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, the email must contain exactly one `@`, be no longer than 254 characters, and have at least one dot and non-empty domain labels after the `@`; the password must contain 12 to 128 characters, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric special character, and contain no whitespace characters. The system stores a sign-in-capable account together with its verified-email status and enters the sign-in page; if the username or email conflicts, any field is missing, the email format is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the password is noncompliant, or the confirmation does not match, the system retains the username and email input, displays an itemized message beside the corresponding field, and does not create an account. The corresponding visible field message contains “Username already exists”, “Username format is invalid”, “Email format is invalid”, “Password requirements are not satisfied”, or “Agree to terms is required”, as applicable. Visitors can use this capability on the account-access page. The system validates input rules, displays field errors, and prevents duplicate accounts; on success, it directly creates an available account. Submitting several invalid fields together must show the username, email, password, and missing-terms messages together, rather than revealing only one error per submission; the submit button remains actionable so these messages can be read. For example, a username beginning with a hyphen, email “not-an-email”, password “short”, confirmation “different”, and unchecked terms produce these field errors and preserve the attempted username. A duplicate username paired with a different unused email displays “Username already exists” and retains both attempted values. A successful registration accepts a unique username, its email, and password; the sign-in form is immediately available, accepts that email, and the resulting signed-in username remains visible after reload.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-sign-up.png)

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: legal slash branches retain selection and nested file context after reload
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
A signed-in user with Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner permission can create a named branch from the current branch head through the branch selector. As the user types, a valid unused name exposes an option named “Create branch: <name>”; selecting it creates the reference and switches the browsing context to the new branch without a second mandatory confirmation. The new branch points to the selected base commit and does not copy files or rewrite the base branch history. Read and Triage users may browse but cannot create branches. Branch names are 1–255 characters and may contain ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, and `/`; names ending in `/` or `.`, containing `..` or `//`, duplicating an existing name, or submitted by an unauthorized user must be rejected. The selector and `Find branch` textbox use the controls defined by REQ-4-3-1. Reloading a successfully created branch preserves it as the selected branch.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: slash branch writes edits and commit history preserve main
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on repository browsing and sign-in provided by REQ-4-1 (Browse Repository Files and Directories) and REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account). From a writable Code page, a contributor can use “Add file” → “Create new file” to add a file on the current branch. Only Write, Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may submit file changes; Read and Triage may browse but may not write. A successful submission creates one commit containing the path, content, commit message, author, parent commit, and target branch, then advances that branch head. The editor exposes a “File name” field, a “File contents” textbox, a “Commit message” field, and a “Commit changes” button. New file paths cannot be empty, start with `/`, contain a `..` path segment, or conflict with an existing file or directory. Commit messages must contain 1–72 non-empty characters after trimming whitespace. Invalid submissions must leave file data, branch head, and commit history unchanged; an invalid path is reported as “Invalid file path”, while a missing message is reported as “Commit message is required”. Seed data provides public repository `file-management-demo` and Write contributor `file-contributor`. A valid unique file such as `pw-file-<unique suffix>.md`, nonempty content, and message `Add <file name>` produce a file view containing the saved content; the file's “Commits” link exposes the submitted message.

Screenshot reference:
![image](reference/github-web-file-editor.png)

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: isolated invalid inputs and duplicate email cannot partially create an account
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
The registration page is the form opened by the unique link named “Create an account” from the sign-in page. The form contains exactly one textbox labeled “Username”, one textbox labeled “Email”, one password input labeled “Password”, one password input labeled “Confirm password”, one initially unchecked checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and one enabled button named “Create account”. The username and email identify the account, while passwords must not be echoed on the page. This product directly marks the email of a successfully registered account as verified and does not provide a subsequent email-verification page. The visitor enters a unique username, email, password, and matching confirmation, checks “Agree to the terms”, and activates “Create account”. The username must consist of 1 to 39 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens (`-`) and must not begin or end with a hyphen; after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, the email must contain exactly one `@`, be no longer than 254 characters, and have at least one dot and non-empty domain labels after the `@`; the password must contain 12 to 128 characters, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric special character, and contain no whitespace characters. The system stores a sign-in-capable account together with its verified-email status and enters the sign-in page; if the username or email conflicts, any field is missing, the email format is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the password is noncompliant, or the confirmation does not match, the system retains the username and email input, displays an itemized message beside the corresponding field, and does not create an account. The corresponding visible field message contains “Username already exists”, “Username format is invalid”, “Email format is invalid”, “Password requirements are not satisfied”, or “Agree to terms is required”, as applicable. Visitors can use this capability on the account-access page. The system validates input rules, displays field errors, and prevents duplicate accounts; on success, it directly creates an available account. Submitting several invalid fields together must show the username, email, password, and missing-terms messages together, rather than revealing only one error per submission; the submit button remains actionable so these messages can be read. For example, a username beginning with a hyphen, email “not-an-email”, password “short”, confirmation “different”, and unchecked terms produce these field errors and preserve the attempted username. A duplicate username paired with a different unused email displays “Username already exists” and retains both attempted values. A successful registration accepts a unique username, its email, and password; the sign-in form is immediately available, accepts that email, and the resulting signed-in username remains visible after reload.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: rejected password preserves old credentials and rejects the candidate
reviewed_behaviors.basis:
This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-1-1-2 (Sign In with an Existing Account); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes. The security form has uniquely labeled password inputs “Current password”, “New password”, and “Confirm password”, and a button “Update password”; submitting an empty current-password field must display the visible application message “Current password is required”. A failure with an incorrect current password and confirmation “does-not-match” must display the corresponding current-password or confirmation error and leave the old credentials usable. Each password-change scenario starts with its own verified account in the stated credential state and a different compliant candidate password. “Password and authentication” is the security page in account Settings used to change the current account credentials; the change affects only the current account's password record and does not alter any other accounts or resources outside the session. The user must provide the current password, a new password compliant with the REQ-1 password rules, and a character-for-character identical confirmation password; all three fields are required. The system validates the change, prevents unauthorized updates, and applies the new password to subsequent sign-in attempts. If the current password is incorrect, the new password is noncompliant, the confirmation does not match, or any field is missing, the system displays the reason in the corresponding field and does not modify the credentials; the applicable visible message is “Current password is incorrect”, “Password confirmation does not match”, or “Current password is required”. The old password remains valid and the new password must not work for sign-in. After a successful update, the page displays “Password updated”, the new password is immediately used for subsequent password-based sign-ins, and the old password must no longer work for new sign-ins.

Seed password-change values are `New-password-456!` for the successful update and
`Required-password-789!` for the missing-current-password scenario.

reviewed_behaviors.behavior: Write/Read/Triage cannot merge; failed required check blocks an approved PR
reviewed_behaviors.basis: On an eligible PR, Merge pull request and then Confirm merge are buttons; confirming displays Merged, and that state remains after reload. A blocked PR keeps a visible disabled Merge pull request button and explains its unmet review or protection condition before any click. Seed data supplies a Maintain account and separate Open PRs for success and refusal. The eligible PR targets protected main, has a current non-author approval and test: success, and has no conflicts. The blocked PR targets a protected branch and lacks the required valid approval; its disabled button is accompanied by Review required by branch protection. The success and refusal states are separate PR records, so neither test relies on restoring a mutation from the other. “Merge” is the only write operation that writes the current compare commit's changes from an Open PR into the base branch; it is not simply marking the PR as complete. Only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge from the PR detail page using the sole supported “Create a merge commit” method; the merge confirmation area should display satisfied and unsatisfied conditions. Before confirmation, the system rereads the target branch head, current compare commit, merge-conflict state, and protection rules — there must be no valid Request changes; if the target is protected, each enabled rule requirement is enforced independently, requiring 1 valid non-author Approve for the current compare commit when Require 1 approval is enabled and requiring `test` success when Require status check test is enabled. An unprotected target has no additional approval-count or check-success requirement, but merging still requires no merge conflicts and no valid Request changes review. After validation succeeds, the system atomically creates a merge commit whose parents are the target-branch head at merge time and the current compare commit, updates the target-branch head, sets the PR to Merged, and stores the merger, time, and resulting commit identifier. If any condition is unsatisfied or persistence fails, the page explains the applicable reason and neither the target branch nor PR changes; a missing required approval displays “Review required by branch protection”. Merged is terminal. This feature builds on the persisted objects, opened pages, or authenticated-session context provided by REQ-6-3-4 (Submit a Pull Request Review) and REQ-6-1 (Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements); it must reuse that context and keep pages and data consistent after the context changes.
